react_result.final_narrative_text: The nine-metabolite differential signature is dominated by arachidonic acid metabolism and eicosanoid biosynthesis, with near-complete cross-paradigm consensus across four independent enrichment tools. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with an FDR of 9.7e-14 and a fold-enrichment of 1430, implicating five input metabolites (15-HETE, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2, arachidonic acid, and leukotriene A4). The same five metabolites recurred in all 14 NSAID/COX-inhibitor action pathways at identical FDR, reflecting their shared biochemical substrate pool. Mummichog's m/z-direct analysis confirmed Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the top network hit (p=0.001) with all 13 overlapping compounds drawn from the m/z network, and Leukotriene metabolism (rank 3, p=0.032) added further specificity for LTA4. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG PSEA listed hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) at rank 0 with 4 overlapping metabolites, confirming the same pathway from the KEGG namespace. Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, rank 1, p=0.008) represented a secondary signal anchored by glycerol and arachidonic acid. The five eicosanoid driver metabolites collectively span the COX pathway (PGJ2, HETEs) and the 5-lipoxygenase branch (LTA4, 5-HETE), suggesting the treatment perturbation activates both major arachidonate catabolic axes simultaneously. The non-lipid metabolites (N-acetylgalactosamine, 2-ketobutyric acid, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) did not achieve significance in any single paradigm and appear as peripheral context metabolites.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The three enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant signal: disruption of the arachidonic acid / eicosanoid network. RaMP ORA placed "Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167)" at rank 0 with an FDR of 9.7×10⁻¹⁴ and a fold-enrichment of 1,430, hitting five driver metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2). Mummichog independently returned "Arachidonic acid metabolism" as the top pathway (p = 0.0015) with an overlap of 13/13 input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00590 first, with four of those same drivers (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE). 2-Ketobutyric acid and glycerol contributed to the fatty-acid and glycerophospholipid sub-themes but did not displace the lipid-oxidative signal as the primary biological story. The six lipid mediators—arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2, and glycerol—all derive from the same 20-carbon phospholipid pool and are sequentially linked: arachidonic acid feeds the 5-lipoxygenase branch (via ALOX5 → 5-HPETE → LTA4) and the cyclooxygenase branch (via PTGS1/2 → PG endoperoxides → PGJ2). N-Acetylgalactosamine and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid do not appear in the eicosanoid-hit list, consistent with their separate amino-sugar and aromatic-acid metabolic niches. All nine input InChIKeys resolved to distinct chemical entities; no structural conflicts were detected. The three-method consensus is robust and specific to the arachidonic acid cascade.

react_result.final_narrative_text:
Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a dominant biological signal: arachidonic acid metabolism and eicosanoid biosynthesis. RaMP-DB ORA identified Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top pathway with FDR = 9.7e-14 (fold enrichment 1430, five input metabolites: 15-HETE, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2, arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4). Mummichog m/z-network analysis ranked Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) first with p = 5.9e-4, mapping five input metabolites into a 13-member empirical network sub-module. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked hsa00590 first (arachidonic acid metabolism) with four metabolites hitting the pathway; 2-oxobutanoate (the anion form of 2-ketobutyric acid) independently hit valine pathway hsa00290 (p = 0.035). Glycerol and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid lacked pathway-level significance across all three tools. N-acetylgalactosamine was resolved to CHEBI:506227 (N-acetyl-D-glucosamine) by mummichog, with the KEGG C01074 annotation flagged for downstream reconciliation. No structural InChIKey conflicts were detected. Arachidonic acid is the primary substrate, bifurcating into the COX/PGJ2 branch and two LOX branches (5-LOX producing leukotriene A4 and 5-HETE; 15-LOX producing 15-HETE). 15-deoxy-PGJ2 signals PPARγ engagement. The 2-ketobutyric acid hit in hsa00290 (valine degradation) provides a minor but orthogonal metabolic node outside the lipid cascade.

Limitations: N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) was annotated by mummichog as N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (KEGG:C00140) due to shared InChIKey first-block; this namespace ambiguity should be resolved before downstream interpretation. Glycerol and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid did not achieve pathway-level significance and may represent background noise or indirect metabolic effects.

payload_summary.fallback_suggested: FELLA R subprocess errored at runtime (currently 'argument is of length zero' on every sub6b-v3 task — W9 D4 stretch target); skip the network/diffusion paradigm and rely on ORA + mummichog
use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

pathway_members.sqlite only indexes HUMAN1 + RECON2; for namespace 'WP', inspect the `metabolites_hit` list inside an EnrichmentResult (e.g. from run_ramp_enrichment) — it carries the method-specific compound roster

Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, rank 1, p=0.008) represented a secondary signal anchored by glycerol and arachidonic acid. The five eicosanoid driver metabolites collectively span the COX pathway (PGJ2, HETEs) and the 5-lipoxygenase branch (LTA4, 5-HETE), suggesting the treatment perturbation activates both major arachidonate catabolic axes simultaneously.
